entry.title: Why Geohazards Must Be Part of the Pacific’s Resilience Agenda
entry.summary:
BANGKOK, Thailand, November 6 (IPS) - For years, global discussions of disaster risk in the Pacific have been dominated by climate change. Rising seas, intensifying cyclones and coastal erosion have rightly captured international attention. This focus, while warranted, should be complemented by greater recognition of geohazards, which are just as consequential and in many cases, more immediately devastating. Addressing this gap requires a more coordinated approach, supported by sustained investment and stronger partnerships, to foster cooperation and strengthen resilience across the Pacific.

Read the full story, “Why Geohazards Must Be Part of the Pacific’s Resilience Agenda”, on globalissues.org →

entry.title: Sixty Years on, UN Is Finally Interpreting Freedom of Association
entry.summary:
GENEVA, November 6 (IPS) - A right under pressure - No one disputes freedom of association. It is in the Constitutions of almost every country, the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, Article 22 of the ICCPR, and in regional Articles in Europe, America, and Africa. What it has never had, at the universal level, is sincere implementation by governments.
